name: Performance Testing and Engineering
certifications: No tool certification required; assessed by a test plan, scripts and a results report
Optional: tool vendor courses for JMeter, k6, Gatling or LoadRunner
tools: APM tool such as Dynatrace, New Relic or Datadog

beginner.summary: For testers, developers and operations staff starting performance testing, independent of one tool. Covers why performance matters, test types, performance requirements, key metrics and percentiles, how load tools work, writing first scripts in k6 and JMeter, think time and pacing, test data, correlation, workload basics, running tests, monitoring the system, reading results, simple bottleneck patterns, front-end performance, test environments, reporting and the performance testing process.
prerequisites: Understands how web applications and APIs work
Has done functional testing or development
Comfortable with a terminal and basic scripting
outcomes: Explain performance test types, requirements and metrics to a team
Write and run simple load tests in k6 and JMeter with realistic data and think time
Monitor the system during a test and recognise common bottlenecks
Plan a small performance test and report its results clearly

days.topic: Performance Testing Overview: Why It Matters and Lab Setup
subtopics: What performance means to users and businesses
Real incidents caused by slow or failing systems
Performance testing compared with functional testing
Who does performance work in a team
Tools in common use: JMeter, k6, Gatling, Locust and LoadRunner
The course application and its monitoring
days.lab_task: Install k6 and JMeter, run a five-user test against the course application with each tool and compare the response times and throughput they report.
days.deliverable: Working tools and a first comparison
checks: Both tools run a test against the course application
Response times from both tools are compared
The value of performance testing is explained with an example

days.topic: Types of Performance Tests: Load, Stress, Spike, Soak and Capacity
subtopics: Choosing test types for a release
days.lab_task: Write load, stress, spike and soak profiles for the course application in k6, run short versions of each and record what each one shows.
days.deliverable: Four load profiles with short-run results
checks: Each test type has a matching load profile
Short versions of all four run
Notes state the risk each type uncovers

days.topic: Performance Requirements and Service Level Objectives
subtopics: Requirements for APIs, pages and batch jobs
days.lab_task: Rewrite five vague performance requirements into measurable objectives using sample analytics, and review them with a role-played product owner.
checks: Each objective has a metric, percentile and target
Targets are based on analytics or business needs
The product owner accepts the objectives

days.topic: Key Metrics: Response Time, Throughput, Errors and Percentiles
subtopics: Latency and time to first byte
days.lab_task: Run a test with mixed fast and slow responses, calculate average, median, 95th and 99th percentiles by hand and explain why the average hides the slow users.
checks: The explanation shows how averages mislead
The slow tail is identified in the histogram

days.topic: How Load Tools Work: Virtual Users, Protocols and Load Generators
subtopics: Virtual users and what they simulate
days.lab_task: Run the same test in closed and open models, watch the load generator's CPU and network, and show when the generator itself becomes the bottleneck.
days.deliverable: Model comparison and generator limits note
checks: Open and closed model results are compared
The point where the generator limits the test is shown

days.topic: First Scripts in k6: HTTP Requests, Checks and Thresholds
days.lab_task: Write a k6 script for login, search and product view with checks and thresholds on the 95th percentile and error rate, and run it with stages.
days.deliverable: k6 script with checks and thresholds
checks: Responses are checked for status and content
Thresholds fail the run when targets are missed
Load ramps through the planned stages

days.topic: First Scripts in JMeter: Thread Groups, Samplers and Assertions
days.lab_task: Build the same journey in JMeter with samplers, assertions and a thread group, run it from the command line and compare results and effort with the k6 version.
days.deliverable: JMeter test plan and tool comparison
checks: The JMeter plan runs the same journey
The test runs from the command line with a report
Effort and results are compared with k6

days.topic: Think Time, Pacing and Realistic User Behaviour
subtopics: Checking that the load is realistic
days.lab_task: Add think time and pacing to the journey in both tools, compare throughput with and without them and check the resulting load against analytics.
checks: Throughput with and without pauses is compared
The load matches analytics within agreed limits

days.topic: Test Data for Load Tests
subtopics: Data that runs out during tests
days.lab_task: Parameterise logins and searches in both tools with generated data, make sure each virtual user uses different data and show the cache effect of reusing the same search.
days.deliverable: Data files, parameterised scripts and cache comparison
checks: Each virtual user uses different data
Data is generated in the needed volume
Reused data gives faster, misleading results

days.topic: Correlation: Handling Tokens, Sessions and Dynamic Values
subtopics: Extracting values in k6 and JMeter
days.lab_task: Find the dynamic values in a recorded checkout, correlate the token and order ID in both tools and prove the script works for twenty users.
checks: Extracted values are used in later requests
Twenty users complete checkout without errors

days.topic: Workload Models: User Mixes and Arrival Rates
subtopics: Journeys and their share of traffic
days.lab_task: Build a workload model from sample analytics with a journey mix and peak arrival rate, check it with Little's law and implement it as k6 scenarios.
checks: The mix and peak rate come from analytics
Little's law confirms the expected concurrency
k6 scenarios produce the modelled rates

days.topic: Running Tests and Watching the System
days.lab_task: Run a planned load test with a pre-test checklist, warm-up and live monitoring, stop it safely when an agreed limit is reached and record the run conditions.
days.deliverable: Run log with conditions and results
checks: The checklist is completed before the run
Live results are monitored during the run
Run conditions and events are logged

days.topic: Monitoring Servers, Databases and Applications During Tests
subtopics: Lining up monitoring with test time
days.lab_task: Set up Prometheus and Grafana for the course application, run a load test, and line up server, database and application metrics with response times.
checks: Server, database and application metrics are captured
Metrics share a time axis with test results
The relationship between load and resource use is described

days.topic: Reading Results and Spotting Common Bottlenecks
days.lab_task: Analyse three result sets with known bottlenecks, match each to its pattern and write a first hypothesis with the evidence that supports it.
checks: Each result set is matched to a bottleneck type
Each analysis proposes what to check next

days.topic: Front-End Performance: Core Web Vitals and Browser Testing
subtopics: Core Web Vitals: LCP, INP and CLS
days.lab_task: Measure Core Web Vitals for three pages, run a small browser-based load with k6 alongside protocol load and report where user-facing time is spent.
checks: Vitals are recorded for three pages
Browser and protocol load run together
User-facing time is broken down by cause

days.topic: API and Microservice Performance Testing
days.lab_task: Load test an API that calls two downstream services, stub one dependency to isolate the API and compare results with and without the real dependency.
days.deliverable: API load results with isolation comparison
checks: The API is load tested end to end
The stubbed run isolates the API's own limits

days.topic: Test Environments and Their Effect on Results
days.lab_task: Compare the test environment with production on five factors, estimate how each affects results and write the limits statement for the test report.
checks: Five factors are compared with production
Each factor's likely effect is stated
The report states what results can predict

days.topic: The Performance Testing Process: Plan, Script, Execute, Analyse and Report
subtopics: Fitting the process into agile delivery
days.lab_task: Map the full performance testing process for a release in a two-week sprint, assign owners for each step and identify where the process usually slips.
days.deliverable: Process map with owners and risks
checks: Every process step has inputs and outputs
Common slips are identified with mitigations

days.topic: Reporting Performance Results Clearly
days.lab_task: Write a performance report from a test run with an executive summary, results against objectives, two bottlenecks, recommendations and a go or no-go statement.
checks: The summary states the outcome in plain words
Results are shown against each objective
Recommendations and go or no-go advice are justified

days.topic: Beginner Capstone: Performance Test of a Web Shop from Plan to Report
days.lab_task: Plan and run a performance test of a web shop: agree objectives, build the workload model, script with data and correlation, run load and stress tests with monitoring, analyse results and present the report.
checks: Load and stress tests complete with monitoring
The report states results, bottlenecks and advice

intermediate.summary: For performance testers who run tests and now need to find causes and work at scale. Covers deeper analysis with APM and tracing, profiling, database performance, caching, JVM and runtime tuning partners, Gatling, Locust, distributed load, cloud load testing, performance testing in CI, baselines and regression detection, mobile back ends, messaging systems, batch jobs, resilience under load, capacity tests, autoscaling, results statistics, test data at scale, security and performance, and performance in agile teams.
prerequisites: Has planned and run performance tests with at least one tool
Reads percentiles, throughput and server metrics
Has reported results to a team
outcomes: Find root causes of performance problems with APM, tracing and profiling
Run distributed and cloud load tests and automate checks in CI
Test databases, caches, messaging, batch and mobile back ends
Detect regressions against baselines and advise on capacity and autoscaling

days.topic: Analysis with APM and Distributed Tracing
subtopics: Correlating traces with load test requests
days.lab_task: Tag load test requests so they can be found in traces, find the slowest spans for a slow journey and present the trace evidence to a role-played developer.
checks: Load test requests are identifiable in traces
The developer agrees the next step

days.topic: Profiling Applications Under Load
days.lab_task: Profile the application under load, read a flame graph to find the hottest code path, take thread dumps at peak and confirm a fix with a retest.
checks: A flame graph is captured under load
The retest shows the fix effect

days.topic: Database Performance Under Load
days.lab_task: Find the three slowest queries during a load test, read their plans, add one index with a DBA and measure the effect on response time and database load.
checks: The three slowest queries are listed with timings
The index change effect is measured

days.topic: Caching and Content Delivery Effects
days.lab_task: Measure response times and hit ratios with cold and warm caches, run a test during cache invalidation and report how much caching hides back-end limits.
checks: Cold and warm results are recorded
The hidden back-end limit is stated

days.topic: Runtime Tuning Partnerships: JVM, .NET and Node.js
subtopics: Changing one setting at a time
When tuning is not the answer
days.lab_task: With a role-played developer, test two garbage collection settings and two thread pool sizes one at a time and record the measured effect of each change.
checks: Effects on percentiles and errors are recorded

days.topic: Gatling for Code-Based Load Tests
subtopics: Gatling simulations in Java or Scala
Comparing Gatling with k6 and JMeter
days.lab_task: Write a Gatling simulation for the shop journey with feeders, checks and an open injection profile, add assertions and compare its report with k6 results.
checks: The simulation runs the planned profile
Assertions fail when targets are missed

days.topic: Locust for Python Teams
subtopics: Running headless and with the web UI
days.lab_task: Write a Locust test with weighted tasks for the shop, run it distributed with two workers and compare effort and results with k6.
checks: Tasks and weights match the workload
Effort and results are compared with k6

days.topic: Distributed Load Generation
subtopics: When one generator is not enough
Distributed modes in k6, JMeter, Gatling and Locust
days.lab_task: Run a distributed test from three generators, monitor them, collect one set of results and show the generators are not the bottleneck.

days.topic: Managed Load Testing Platforms in the Cloud
subtopics: Grafana Cloud k6, Azure Load Testing and similar
days.lab_task: Run the shop test from a managed service in two regions, reach a private environment through its network options and compare cost and effort with self-hosted generators.
checks: The test runs from two regions

days.topic: Performance Checks in CI Pipelines
subtopics: Fast performance checks on every change
days.lab_task: Add a short k6 check with thresholds to the pipeline, schedule a nightly larger test, publish trends and show a deliberate slowdown failing the build.
checks: The short check fails on a deliberate slowdown
The nightly test runs and publishes trends
Developers receive the result on their change

days.topic: Baselines and Regression Detection
days.lab_task: Create a baseline from three repeat runs, compare a new build automatically, flag a regression beyond the noise and record its cause.
checks: Variation between repeat runs is measured
The regression is flagged beyond the noise

days.topic: Mobile Back-End and Network Conditions
subtopics: Payload size and number of calls
days.lab_task: Model mobile traffic for the shop API, run tests with simulated 4G and slow networks and report how payload size and call count affect mobile users.
checks: Results are recorded for two network conditions
Payload and call count effects are explained

days.topic: Messaging Systems and Event Streams Under Load
tools: k6 or a messaging load tool
days.lab_task: Load a message broker with producers at rising rates, measure consumer lag and throughput, find the point where lag grows without recovering and report it.
checks: Producer rates rise through planned steps
Consumer lag is recorded at each step

days.topic: Batch Jobs and Data Pipeline Performance
days.lab_task: Run a nightly batch job with current and doubled data volumes alongside light online traffic and report whether it still fits its window.
days.deliverable: Batch test results and risk report
checks: Durations are recorded for both volumes
Online response times during the job are recorded
The batch window risk is stated

days.topic: Resilience Under Load: Failures, Timeouts and Retries
days.lab_task: Stop an instance and slow a dependency during a load test, measure errors and recovery time and report whether timeouts and retries behaved as designed.
checks: Faults are injected at planned times
Errors and recovery time are recorded
Behaviour is compared with the design

days.topic: Capacity Tests and Autoscaling Behaviour
days.lab_task: Measure throughput per instance, test autoscaling under a steady ramp and a spike, record scale-out delays and calculate cost per transaction.
checks: Scale-out delays are recorded for ramp and spike

days.topic: Statistics for Performance Results
subtopics: Outliers and what to do with them
days.lab_task: Analyse five repeat runs, calculate variation and confidence in the 95th percentile, compare two builds properly and write the conclusion with its uncertainty.
checks: The build comparison accounts for variation

days.topic: Test Data at Scale and Production-Like Volumes
subtopics: Data effects on caches and indexes
days.lab_task: Generate production-like data volumes with realistic distribution, run the same test on small and large data and report the difference.
checks: Volumes and distribution match the target
Results on small and large data are compared

days.topic: Performance Work in Agile Teams
subtopics: Performance in the definition of done
days.lab_task: Add performance acceptance criteria to three stories, run small tests within the sprint and present performance status in a role-played sprint review.
days.deliverable: Stories, sprint tests and review notes
checks: Small tests run before the stories close
Performance status is shown in the review

days.topic: Intermediate Capstone: Root Cause Investigation and Regression Gate
days.lab_task: Investigate a slow release: run a distributed test, trace and profile the slow journey, find the database or cache cause, verify the fix with a retest and add a baseline gate to CI.
days.deliverable: Investigation evidence, retest results and CI gate
checks: The root cause is supported by traces and profiles
The CI gate catches the same regression

advanced.summary: For performance engineers, SREs and architects who own performance across systems. Covers performance engineering as a discipline, SLOs and error budgets, architecture reviews, performance modelling and queueing, capacity planning, cost and performance, observability-led engineering, testing in production, chaos engineering, large-scale events, performance of AI and LLM services, data platforms, mainframe and legacy systems, enterprise protocols, tool strategy, governance, team building and troubleshooting.
prerequisites: Has led performance testing for releases and found root causes with developers
Understands architecture, monitoring and cloud infrastructure
Works with operations and product leaders
outcomes: Lead performance engineering with SLOs, models and capacity plans
Test and improve performance in production safely with observability and chaos experiments
Prepare systems for major events and new workloads such as AI services
Set tool strategy, governance and team practices for performance

days.topic: Performance Engineering as a Discipline
subtopics: Design, build, test, release and operate
Shared responsibility with development and operations
days.lab_task: Assess an organisation's performance maturity across the lifecycle, set performance budgets for two products and present an improvement roadmap.
checks: Each lifecycle stage has a maturity rating

days.topic: SLOs, Error Budgets and Release Decisions
days.lab_task: Define SLOs and an error budget policy for two services, connect pre-release test results to them and make a release decision for a build that uses half the budget.
days.deliverable: SLOs, budget policy and release decision
checks: The release decision follows the policy

days.topic: Architecture Reviews for Performance and Scalability
days.lab_task: Review a proposed architecture, estimate peak load per component, identify the top five scalability risks and design tests that target them.
days.deliverable: Review findings and targeted test plan
checks: Five risks are identified with reasons
Each risk has a targeted test

days.topic: Performance Modelling with Queueing Theory
subtopics: Little's law and the utilisation law
days.lab_task: Build a simple queueing model of a three-tier service from test data, validate it against a new test and use it to answer two what-if questions.
checks: The model uses measured service times
Predictions match a new test within limits
Two what-if questions are answered with the model

days.topic: Capacity Planning for Growth
subtopics: Inputs: forecasts, tests and production data
Reviewing plans with operations and finance
days.lab_task: Build a twelve-month capacity plan with headroom and triggers for a service and its database, review it with role-played operations and finance and agree tracking.
checks: The plan covers the service and its dependencies
Operations and finance agree triggers and costs
Tracking against the plan is set up

days.topic: Cost and Performance Trade-Offs in the Cloud
days.lab_task: Test three deployment options for a service, calculate cost per transaction and SLO compliance for each and recommend the best trade-off to role-played FinOps and product owners.
checks: Three options are tested under the same load
Cost and SLO compliance are calculated

days.topic: Observability-Led Performance Engineering
subtopics: Metrics, logs, traces and profiles together
days.lab_task: Investigate a production-style slowdown from telemetry alone, form and test two hypotheses and write an investigation playbook for the team.
checks: Telemetry evidence is gathered across signals
Each hypothesis is confirmed or rejected
The playbook covers the steps used

days.topic: Testing in Production Safely
days.lab_task: Design a production performance test with shadow traffic or a controlled load window, approvals, a kill switch and a communication plan, and run a small version.
days.deliverable: Production test plan and small run results
checks: Approvals and kill switch are in place

days.topic: Chaos Engineering for Performance and Resilience
days.lab_task: Run a game day with three chaos experiments under load, measure steady state deviation and recovery and turn the findings into fixes and automated experiments.
days.deliverable: Game day record, findings and automated experiment
checks: Each experiment has a steady state hypothesis

days.topic: Preparing for Major Events and Peak Traffic
subtopics: Sales, launches and exam results days
Load tests at peak and beyond
days.lab_task: Prepare a system for a sales event: forecast the peak, run a readiness review, test at peak and beyond, write the runbook and run a role-played war room.
days.deliverable: Forecast, readiness review, test results and runbook
checks: The peak forecast uses past data
Peak and beyond-peak tests pass or have mitigations
The runbook and war room roles are ready

days.topic: Performance of AI and LLM-Based Services
subtopics: How LLM services differ: tokens, latency and streaming
Time to first token and tokens per second
Concurrency and rate limits of model providers
Caching and batching for LLM calls
days.lab_task: Load test an LLM-backed feature in a sandbox, measure time to first token, tokens per second, errors and cost at three concurrency levels and report limits and costs.
checks: Time to first token and throughput are recorded
Rate limit and error behaviour is recorded

days.topic: Data Platform and Analytics Performance
days.lab_task: Test a set of BI dashboards with concurrent users against a warehouse, measure query times and cost, change partitioning for one table and measure the effect.
days.deliverable: Analytics performance results and change effect
checks: Dashboard query times are measured under concurrency
The partitioning change effect is measured

days.topic: Legacy, Mainframe and Enterprise Application Performance
days.lab_task: Plan a performance test for an ERP transaction path that includes a legacy back end, choose protocols and tools, and identify the monitoring needed from legacy teams.
checks: Protocol and tool choices are justified
Licence and access constraints are handled

days.topic: Tool Strategy for Performance Testing
days.lab_task: Compare four performance tools for an organisation's needs, calculate three-year cost and write a tool strategy that allows team choice within standards.
checks: Tools are compared on agreed criteria
The strategy balances standards and team choice

days.topic: Governance and Standards for Performance Work
subtopics: Standards for scripts, data and reports
Approvals for large and production tests
days.lab_task: Write standards and approval rules for performance work, review three existing tests against them and define release gates.
checks: Standards cover scripts, data, runs and reports
Three tests are reviewed and fixed

days.topic: Building a Performance Engineering Team
days.lab_task: Design a performance engineering team with roles, an engagement model, a hiring exercise and a training plan, and present how its impact will be measured.
days.deliverable: Team design, hiring exercise and training plan
checks: The engagement model explains how teams get help

days.topic: Performance Engineering for Platform Teams
days.lab_task: Test a shared platform with two tenants where one creates heavy load, measure the noisy neighbour effect, propose quotas and test them.
days.deliverable: Multi-tenant test results and quota proposal
checks: The noisy neighbour effect is quantified
Quotas reduce the effect in a retest

days.topic: Sustainability and Energy Efficiency in Performance
days.lab_task: Measure resource use per transaction for two versions of a service, estimate their energy and carbon impact and recommend changes that keep SLOs.
checks: Resource use per transaction is measured
Energy and carbon estimates are calculated
Changes keep SLOs while reducing use

days.topic: Troubleshooting Hard Performance Problems
subtopics: Problems that only appear at scale
days.lab_task: Work through two hard performance cases (an intermittent tail latency spike and a scale-only failure), eliminate causes systematically and document the investigation.
checks: Causes are ruled out with evidence
The confirmed causes are supported by data
Lessons are written for the team

days.topic: Advanced Capstone: Performance Engineering Plan for a Critical Platform
days.lab_task: Write and present a performance engineering plan for a critical platform with SLOs, architecture review findings, capacity and cost plans, production testing and chaos plans and a team and governance model.
checks: SLOs and budgets exist for critical services
Capacity and cost plans are evidence-based
objectives: Plan performance for a critical platform
